targetText: All that was formerly produced in the bosom of the family is now being manufactured on a mass scale in workshops and factories. The machine has superseded the wife.
explanation: Historical shift in production: industrial capitalism stripped the domestic home of its self-contained manufacturing role, socialization of production into factories.

targetText: The family no longer produces; it only consumes. The housework that remains consists of cleaning, cooking, washing, and mending. These are difficult and exhausting tasks, but this work is different in one important way from the work our grandmothers did: these four tasks are of no value to the state and the national economy, for they do not create any new values or make any contribution to the prosperity of the country.
explanation: Under industrial capitalism, domestic labor is reduced to non-productive, repetitive chores that absorb women's energy without creating recognized exchange-value, isolating women within individual households.

targetText: Instead of the working woman having to struggle with the cooking in the kitchen, communist society will organise public restaurants and communal kitchens.
explanation: Socialization of domestic work: replacing private isolated kitchens and laundries with high-quality public dining halls, central laundries, and repair centers frees women from domestic servitude.
